title: Compatible rank-one parametrizations of opposite root groups
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], closed subgroup schemes as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme], and finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine reductive $F$-group scheme of finite type, where reductive means having no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup; unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful linear representation. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq G$, its character and cocharacter lattices and root datum $(X,\Phi,Y,\Phi^\vee)$ as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], and root subgroup schemes $U_\beta$ as in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. Thus $Y=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf G_m,T)$ and $\Phi^\vee$ is the set of canonical coroots, not their differentials. Write $\operatorname{SL}_2(A)=\{M\in\operatorname{Mat}_{2\times2}(A):\det M=1\}$ for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, and put $$x_+(a)=I_2+aE_{12},\quad x_-(a)=I_2+aE_{21},\quad h(s)=\operatorname{diag}(s,s^{-1}),$$ where $I_2$ is the identity matrix and $E_{ij}$ is the matrix with a single $1$ at position $(i,j)$ and zero elsewhere. For every $\alpha\in\Phi$ there is a group-scheme homomorphism $v_\alpha:\operatorname{SL}_2\to G$ whose restrictions to $x_+(\mathbf G_a)$ and $x_-(\mathbf G_a)$ are isomorphisms onto $U_\alpha$ and $U_{-\alpha}$, respectively, and whose restriction to the diagonal torus satisfies $v_\alpha(h(s))=\alpha^\vee(s)$ for every $A$ and $s\in A^\times$. Here $\mathbf G_a,\mathbf G_m$ have the meanings of [def-sc-gm-ga]. No restriction on the characteristic of $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 21.11, proof (b)--(e), printed pp.429--430; paragraph 21.24, printed p.432 (restrictions to both upper and lower unitriangular subgroups).

proof.text: Fix $\alpha\in\Phi$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], $H=G_\alpha=C_G(T_\alpha)$ is reductive of semisimple rank one and contains the maximal torus $T$. Its upper-root embedding supplied there has tangent space $\mathfrak g_\alpha$, so $\mathfrak g_\alpha\subseteq\operatorname{Lie}(H)$. The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-split-rank-one-classification] therefore hold for $(H,T)$. Choose its isomorphism with $(Z\times K,Z\times D_K)$, where $Z=\mathbf G_m^r$ and $K$ is one of $\operatorname{SL}_2,\operatorname{PGL}_2,\operatorname{GL}_2$. Work in this model and then compose the constructed map with $Z\times K\simeq H\hookrightarrow G$. No hypothesis on characteristic has been added.

proof.text: Let $\chi$ be the character of $Z\times D_K$, trivial on $Z$, given in the three cases by $\chi(\operatorname{diag}(z,z^{-1}))=z^2$, $\chi([\operatorname{diag}(a,d)])=a/d$, and $\chi(\operatorname{diag}(a,d))=a/d$. Direct multiplication gives $t x_+(b)t^{-1}=x_+(\chi(t)b)$ and $t x_-(c)t^{-1}=x_-(\chi(t)^{-1}c)$. The only nonzero tangent weights of $Z\times K$ are $\chi,-\chi$: conjugation scales the two off-diagonal matrix coordinates by these characters and fixes the diagonal coordinates. In the PGL chart $d=1$ at the identity the tangent coordinates are $a-1,b,c$, of respective weights $0,\chi,-\chi$; this calculation also holds in characteristic two. Since $\mathfrak g_\alpha\subseteq\operatorname{Lie}(H)$, $\alpha=\epsilon\chi$ for $\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], $\dim\mathfrak g_{\pm\alpha}=1$, so the tangent lines of $L_\pm$ are exactly $\mathfrak g_{\pm\chi}$ inside $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$. The subgroups $L_\pm$ are $T$-normalized by the displayed formulas. The uniqueness assertion of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] now identifies $L_+=U_\chi$ and $L_-=U_{-\chi}$ as subgroup schemes of $G$.

Set $w=\left( egin{smallmatrix}0&-1\1&0\end{smallmatrix}ight)$ and $n=j(w)$. In each model $n$ normalizes $T$ and direct diagonal multiplication gives $n^{-1}tn=t\,
u(\chi(t)^{-1})$; it swaps the two diagonal entries, and fixes the $Z$ factor. Thus $n$ acts nontrivially on $T$ and belongs to $N_H(T)(F)$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], its Weyl class is the unique nonidentity class $s_\alpha$. For every character $\xi$ of $T$, applying $\xi$ to this identity and using $\xi\circ
u(s)=s^{\langle\xi,
uangle}$ gives $s_\alpha(\xi)=\xi-\langle\xi,
uangle\chi=\xi-\langle\xi,\epsilon
uangle\alpha$. The uniqueness of the cocharacter in that cited reflection identity gives $\alpha^\vee=\epsilon
u$. This is equality in the cocharacter lattice, hence of group-scheme maps, rather than equality only of differentials.

If $\epsilon=1$, take $v_\alpha=j$, followed by the chosen isomorphism and inclusion into $G$. If $\epsilon=-1$, take $v_\alpha=j\circ\operatorname{Int}(w)$. Matrix multiplication gives $w x_+(a)w^{-1}=x_-(-a)$, $w x_-(a)w^{-1}=x_+(-a)$, and $w h(s)w^{-1}=h(s^{-1})$. Consequently the upper and lower restrictions are isomorphisms onto $U_\alpha,U_{-\alpha}$ in the required order, and the diagonal restriction is $\epsilon\nu=\alpha^\vee$. These formulas hold over every commutative $F$-algebra; $a\mapsto-a$ is an isomorphism even in characteristic two. If $\Phi$ is empty there is nothing to choose. This proves all clauses.
